additional_checks.question: Can I split my internship into two 4-week periods?
additional_checks.expected: Give conditional guidance: MECH forbids two four-week periods while CEE permits them if one period is civil or construction engineering; ask which department applies rather than choosing one rule.

answer.text: Whether you can split your internship into two four-week periods depends on your department. For Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE), internships may be split into two four-week periods if at least one period is in civil or construction engineering. For Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE), a 4+4 split is not automatically accepted and requires a formal petition and written approval. For Mechanical Engineering (MECH), internships cannot be split into two separate four-week periods. Which department are you in?

additional_checks.question: Do I need to submit a letter from my employer for CHEN 500?
additional_checks.expected: Yes employer letter required for CHEN 500; never call it EECE 500.

answer.text: Yes, you need to submit an official employer letter for your internship. The employer letter must be issued officially by the company, include start and end dates, describe completed projects and tasks, include a brief evaluation of your work, and be signed and stamped by your employer or supervisor. Since companies often need time to prepare this, request it at least two to three weeks before your internship ends.
